text:
maria: Heads-up — our regional GPU healthscore looks artificially high for ap-southeast. Grafana shows near-0 ECC/XID rates there despite multiple replacement jobs. Could be a telemetry gap.

devon: I saw that too. ap-southeast-hosts have replace jobs succeeding but the 'gpu_xid_errors_total' panel stays flat. Other regions spike as expected.

ash: Possible causes: nvml-exporter version mismatch, prometheus scrape relabeling, or metrics not being scraped from driver pods. Did we change scrape config recently for that k8s cluster?

maria: I checked. Scrape intervals were changed to 60s in a rollout last week (should be 15s). Also node label for region was mis-annotated on ~30 nodes -> aggregation grouped them under an old region tag.

sre_jack: That explains the flat line — aggregation used region label so errors were attributed elsewhere. Two quick fixes: revert scrape interval and fix node annotations. But we should also hard-validate exporter versions; older nvml-exporter doesn't emit ECC counters consistently.

devon: Agreed. Quick commands I ran:

```
# find nodes with wrong label
kubectl get nodes --selector='node.kubernetes.io/region!=ap-southeast' -o wide | grep ap-southeast

# check exporter version
kubectl -n gpu get pods -l app=nvml-exporter -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.spec.containers[0].image}\n{end}'
```

ash: We should also update the Grafana query to be robust to gaps. For XID spikes use:

```
increase(gpu_xid_errors_total[5m])
```

and then use max_over_time(increase(...)[15m:5m]) to catch bursts across scrapes.

maria: Good call. On the healthscore algorithm: current weighted sum is too naive. Proposing change to use exponential decay on recent errors and normalize by GPU-uptime-per-card. Rough sketch:

- ECC rate (last 30m) * 0.5
- XID spikes (peak increases last 15m) * 0.3
- Memory-correctable errors per-card * 0.2
- Apply exp decay with 10m half-life so old blips fade

ash: Sounds reasonable. Also add a metric that flags repeated drains/replacements per-card in 24h — that should bump priority even if raw error count is low (flaky card indicator).

sre_jack: For alerts/SLOs: we currently target 99.9% per-region. Given telemetry uncertainty, propose temporary adjustments:

- Alert channel: page on region-level healthscore < 99.5% (P1)
- Warning (non-page) for 99.5% <= health < 99.9%
- Runbook: If page, check exporter versions, node labels, then cordon+drain suspected nodes and swap GPUs if HW team available.

devon: Cost note — aggressive replacements (RMAs) across region increase spare pool use and cross-region capacity spikes. We should prefer draining and isolating cards first and only RMA after reproducible ECC/XID confirmation over 3 separate windows.

maria: Agreed. Action items:
1) devon: revert scrape interval rollout in ap-southeast and patch exporter to v0.6.2 (why we chose that earlier)
2) ash: update Grafana panels/queries and add max_over_time-based burst detection
3) sre_jack: add flaky-card metric (replacements_count[24h]) and update healthscore formula in dashboard
4) maria: temporary SLO/alert thresholds doc and postmortem template

ops-bot: Incident alert (automated): "gpu-healthscore ap-southeast dropped from 99.98% to 99.47% — potential telemetry mismatch" (ts: 1876543228)

devon: I'll start the revert now and report back when scrapes resume. If anyone wants the drain script I used earlier:

```
# cordon + safe drain (ignore daemonsets)
kubectl cordon $NODE
kubectl drain $NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
# mark node GPU as unschedulable in inventory
kubectl label node $NODE gpu-status=isolated --overwrite
```

ash: Once metrics flow again, we'll rerun the healthscore backtest over last 7 days to check sensitivity.

maria: Thanks team. Please add small notes in the incident channel and link the dashboard after changes. We'll decide on RMAs after two sustained windows of confirmed XID/ECC activity.

sre_jack: I'll open a follow-up thread with the proposed healthscore formula and sample PromQL for review.

maria: thanks — ping me when dashboards PRs are up :thumbsup:"
